title: fig05 extended with full area-pairwise contrasts (bug found+fixed) and a stimulus-window counterpart, per user request
notes: User asked: since fig05 already has all-band power vs V1, why not also show one-area-to-others (full pairwise, not just vs V1) and both omission-vs-baseline and stim-vs-baseline versions, in fig05 and its supplements.

Refactored the Model F (area+subject additive GLMM) and its new pairwise-contrast logic out of fit_omission_band_power_glmm.py into a shared module, scripts/area_subject_glmm.py -- specifically to avoid a third instance of the exact duplicated-logic-drift bug pattern already found twice this session (bh() and area pooling, both in fit_omission_band_power_glmm.py). Verified the refactor reproduces byte-identical numbers to the pre-refactor inline version before trusting it.

Added all-pairwise-area-contrast computation: for a given Model F fit, every area-pair difference (not just each area vs the reference V1) is recoverable as a linear contrast of the SAME fitted coefficients via res.t_test(contrast) -- no refitting per pair. Caught a REAL bug while building this: the contrast vector was constructed backwards relative to its own term label (labeled 'B - A' but the vector actually computed 'A - B'). Found via a sign sanity check -- a pairwise contrast against the reference area should exactly reproduce that area's already-known Model F coefficient, and it didn't, until fixed. This is exactly the kind of check this project's own doctrine calls for ('verify a design/computation, don't assume').

Also caught and fixed a second, independent sign bug in fig05_v1_area_hierarchy_glmm.py's own matrix-drawing code (draw_pairwise_grid), found by tracing through both fixes together before trusting a rendered figure -- confirmed the final combination (fixed contrast + matrix-drawing sign logic) reproduces Model F's own vs-V1 coefficients exactly via direct numeric spot-check, not just visual plausibility.

New supplement: fig05_v1_area_hierarchy_glmm/svg/fig05_supp_pairwise_omission.svg -- all C(10,2)=45 area pairs x 5 bands = 225 tests, declared as its OWN family (a different question from the main figure's 45-test vs-V1 family). 8/225 survive Holm-Bonferroni, 34/225 survive BH-FDR. Registered as figS31 in build_supplements.py's PLAN.

New stimulus-window census: scripts/compute_stim_channel_band_power_census.py -- real-stimulus (RRRR/AAAB/BBBA) counterpart to compute_channel_band_power_census_v2.py's omission census, identical measure/window/baseline convention (dB relative to the same -250..-50ms pre-onset baseline), slots 2/3/4 matching the omission side's coverage. Full corpus run (303 files x 3 slots) launched in background; ~55 min estimated based on the omission census's own runtime at comparable scale.

New scripts/fit_stim_band_power_glmm.py: calls the SAME shared area_subject_glmm.fit_area_subject_and_pairwise() on the stimulus census, giving a directly comparable area x band (and full pairwise) result for 'is a real stimulus different across areas' -- not yet run pending the census finishing.
issues: Stimulus-side GLMM and figures not yet built as of this node -- waiting on the background census extraction.

Once the stimulus GLMM completes, fig05's figure/supplement panels need extending to show the stim-window results alongside the existing omission-window ones (main figure could gain a second heatmap, or the stim results could be entirely supplement-only -- not yet decided).
plan: Once outputs/lfp_band_census_stim/channel_band_power.csv.gz finishes, run fit_stim_band_power_glmm.py, then extend fig05_v1_area_hierarchy_glmm.py to draw the stim-window vs-V1 heatmap and pairwise matrix as new supplement panels (or main-figure companions), register any new panels in build_supplements.py's PLAN.

verification.receipt: scripts/area_subject_glmm.py (shared module + bug fix); context/figures/fig05_v1_area_hierarchy_glmm/svg/fig05_supp_pairwise_stats.csv (225 rows); direct numeric sanity check matching V3a/d-V1 beta = +1.112686 exactly.
verification.verdict: verified (omission side); stimulus side in progress
